subject: removal pass: audit what earns its place against a RECORDED failure — rework ledger, out-of-band ledger, boundary lint, two-sample gate, time-aware caps all landed inside 72h

notes.text: AUDIT RESULT — little to remove, and that is the honest finding rather than a failure to look. Every recent addition traces to a RECORDED failure: rework ledger (owner reported caught-mistakes being narrated as wins), out-of-band log + ⛔ ruled-out (the Apple/AWS incident, where a twice-confirmed component was re-investigated), boundary lint (CI red TWICE from fixtures pinned on a threshold), two-sample gate (a rate-limit reading measured swinging 82→61→82 in ~20s), section-naming in the gate (a red verdict printed with no cause), drain→burn-down wiring (the owner woke to an idle queue). The two WEAKEST by this standard are preventive rather than reactive: R91's foreign-repo matrix (no defect found — it pins a promise R1/R9 had been making untested) and the time-aware branch cap (an owner decision for a week AFK, not a failure). Neither is worth deleting: both are tests or a constant. GENUINELY DEAD: matching_files in tq, which dies with export/import (#16), and six orphaned state directories on disk. Manufacturing further deletions to make this pass look productive would be the opposite of its point.
